title: Chapter 67: Soft 5
content:
Chapter 67

The woman added, "I just hope he knows who his real enemies are. If he wants revenge, he should go after those high-and-mighty cultivators. Just leave ordinary folks like us out of it."

"Who knows with a guy like him?" her husband replied. "I was just a kid when he slaughtered over three thousand people at Qishan, but I still remember—it wasn't just the cultivators who were terrified. Regular families were scared out of their minds, too. The man's a bloodthirsty monster with no regard for kith or kin."

The smile completely faded from Wei Wuxian's face.

Moments ago, he had been listening to the couple's quiet domestic chatter with lighthearted amusement. Now, his head suddenly felt like it weighed a thousand pounds. He couldn't bring himself to lift it, terrified of seeing the expression on Lan Wangji's face. Whatever the couple said after that became nothing more than silent background noise.

Just then, a terrifying, guttural roar shattered the quiet night. The family inside had been eating and chatting happily, but the inhuman screech startled them so badly that a dish shattered on the floor, and the toddler burst into tears. The young man grabbed a hoe, shouting, "Don't panic! I've got this!"

Even Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji shifted slightly, startled by the noise. Lan Wangji moved to stand up, but Wei Wuxian felt a sudden pang of intuition. He grabbed the front of Lan Wangji's robes, whispering, "Don't move."

Lan Wangji’s eyes widened slightly. Whatever made that roar was clearly a vicious, bloodthirsty creature; if the young farmer faced it alone, he was a dead man. Yet Wei Wuxian repeated firmly, "Don't move."

A woman's scream echoed from the yard, followed by an even louder, monstrous roar right outside the door. The creature was already inside. Lan Wangji couldn't sit by any longer—Bichen unsheathed in a flash of blinding light, just as the family of three sprinted out the front door, screaming as they fled into the night. Bichen’s sword-aura sliced through the haystack, sending straw flying everywhere.

Through the swirling debris stood a pitch-black figure. With matted, disheveled hair, bared teeth, and random twigs protruding from its body, the creature looked equal parts terrifying and utterly ridiculous. Lan Wangji, having never seen such an odd creature, paused for a fraction of a second.

Wei Wuxian spoke up first, sighing, "Wen Ning, it's been years since you last cleared your throat, but your roar is getting scarier by the day."

The pitch-black "monster" opened its mouth, sounding thoroughly sheepish. "Master... Iama fierce corpse, after all. That's just how we sound..."

Wei Wuxian patted his shoulder encouragingly. "Very fierce. Full of presence."

Wen Ning cast a quick glance at Lan Wangji. Remembering that the Gusu Lan Clan had a strict aversion to unkempt appearances, he nervously tried to smooth down his wild hair. Seeing him covered in mud and bristling with twigs, Wei Wuxian grimaced, plucking a stray branch from his head. "Why'd you burst out like that? And what's with the look—did you get mugged? What on earth did you smear on your face?"

"It's just dirt and mud from the ground..." Wen Ning muttered, lowering his head. "I saw you two go inside and not come out for a long time..."

"You've been following us?"

Wen Ning nodded, and the pieces clicked into place for Wei Wuxian. Knowing he couldn't show his face to anyone else, Wen Ning had been tailing them quietly after they left Cloud Recesses. When he saw them disappear into the farmhouse for so long, he crept closer to eavesdrop. Hearing the couple badmouth Wei Wuxian made him feel awkward and uncomfortable, so he decided to scare the family off to give his master and Lan Wangji a way out. Fearing his usual face wasn't intimidating enough, he had plastered himself in mud and foliage.

Wei Wuxian almost choked on a laugh, while Wen Ning stood there flushing with embarrassment, desperately wiping the mud off his face. But as he did, Wei Wuxian noticed dark stains on his hands. "Wait. What's that?"

"Oh, it's nothing..." Wen Ning stammered.

Lan Wangji’s eyes narrowed. "Blood."

Only then did Wei Wuxian catch the metallic tang clinging to Wen Ning. His heart sank. Seeing his reaction, Wen Ning frantically waved his hands. "No, no! It's not live blood! I mean, it's blood, but not from the living!"

"Not from the living? You fought something?"

Wen Ning led them deeper down the path into a wild, untamed forest. Scattered across the clearing were twenty or thirty freshly dug graves, alongside a half-excavated pit. Beside the pit lay a pile of corpses—or rather, a pile of body parts. Kneeling down to inspect them, Wei Wuxian saw severed arms still flexing their fingers and detached heads furiously grinding their teeth with sickly crunching noises. They had already turned.

"You really chopped them up, didn't you?" Wei Wuxian remarked.

"If I didn't mince them, they'd keep trying to bite people," Wen Ning explained helplessness. "I couldn't stop them otherwise. There are fierce corpses like this all along the road..."

"All along the road? You've been clearing the path ahead of us this whole time?"

Wen Ning gave a meek nod. Being a fierce corpse himself, his ability to sense his own kind was far sharper and wider in range than any living cultivator's. That explained why their journey had been so unnervingly peaceful. Wei Wuxian had wondered why they hadn't encountered a single corpse despite rumors of hordes gathering near Yiling; turns out Wen Ning had been sweeping the roads clean ahead of them.

"When did you start tailing us?" Wei Wuxian asked.

Lan Wangji spoke up quietly, "Since Carp Tower."

Wei Wuxian looked over in surprise.

"The day the sects ambushed us," Lan Wangji added, "he lent a hand."

Wei Wuxian let out a long sigh. "Didn't I tell you to find a safe place to hide and stay out of trouble?"

Wen Ning offered a bitter, hollow smile. "But Master... where else could I possibly go?"

Once upon a time, he had a home to return to and people to follow. But now, in this vast world, everyone except Wei Wuxian was a complete stranger.

After a moment of heavy silence, Wei Wuxian stood up, dusting off his robes. "Let's bury them."

Wen Ning nodded hastily and went back to digging the half-finished pit. Lan Wangji drew Bichen, channeling a burst of spiritual energy that blasted a clean, deep trench into the earth.

Wei Wuxian raised an eyebrow. "Hanguang-jun, you're digging graves now, too?"

Lan Wangji turned around to reply, but before he could speak, Wen Ning stepped up behind him. Stiffening his face, the corpse forced his rigid mouth into what he clearly hoped was a polite smile. "...Young Master Lan, do you need help? I've already finished my side."

Lan Wangji glanced behind him. A neat row of dark, perfectly uniform pits lined the forest floor, flanked by pristine mounds of dirt.

Maintaining his terrifying "smile," Wen Ning added eagerly, "I do this a lot. I have plenty of experience. It'll be fast."

As forwhohad made him "do this a lot," the answer went without saying.

After a beat of silence, Lan Wangji said, "No need. You can go help..."

Before he could finish his sentence, he realized Wei Wuxian hadn't moved an inch. He was crouched nearby, watching them like a spectator at a show. He was holding the watermelon he’d swiped from the farmhouse, staring at it intently as if pondering the most efficient way to carve it up.

Meeting Lan Wangji’s unreadable gaze, Wei Wuxian offered an innocent smile. "Now, Hanguang-jun, don't look at me like that! I'm empty-handed and my spiritual energy is practically nonexistent, remember? Everyone has their own specialty! When it comes to digging graves, he's the expert. Why don't we figure out how to eat this melon instead? Bichen just touched grave dirt, so it's out of commission for food prep. Do either of you have a spare blade on you?"

Wen Ning shook his head. "Sorry... I didn't bring one."

Wei Wuxian turned his eyes back to Lan Wangji. "Hanguang-jun... what about Suibian? Is it in your pouch?"

Without a word, Lan Wangji pulled Suibian from his Qiankun sleeve. Wei Wuxian scooped up the melon in one hand and the sword in the other. With a flick of his wrist, he flashed a graceful sword-flower, slicing the watermelon into eight neat wedges. Once done, he plopped right back down on the ground, happily munching on a slice while watching the two of them dig like dutiful laborers.

Within the time it took for an incense stick to burn, Wen Ning had dug a fresh row of identical pits. As he carefully placed the dismembered body parts inside, he murmured apologetically, "I'm so sorry, everyone. I can't really tell whose arm belongs to whom anymore. If I mix any of you up, please don't hold it against me..."

Once the melon was devoured and the corpses were buried, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji set off again.

A few days later, they arrived in Yiling.

The Burial Mounds lay less than three miles outside the small town. Though they had no idea what was waiting for them at the top, Wei Wuxian’s gut told him it was going to be bad news.

Yet with Lan Wangji walking beside him—his steps calm, his expression serene—Wei Wuxian couldn't muster a shred of anxiety. Walking through the familiar streets of Yiling, surrounded by the warm, recognizable local dialect, he felt thoroughly refreshed. Even though he wasn't buying anything, he couldn't resist striking up conversations with the street vendors in the local tongue just for the joy of it.

Satisfied, he turned his donkey around. "Hanguang-jun, do you remember this town?"

Lan Wangji gave a subtle nod. "I do."

Wei Wuxian grinned. "I knew your memory was better than mine! We ran into each other right here once. You were out in Yiling on a night-hunt, and I offered to buy you dinner. Remember that?"

"I remember."

Wei Wuxian chuckled. "Though I have to admit, you ended up footing the bill anyway. Haha!"

Sitting cross-legged on Little Apple as the donkey trotted along, Wei Wuxian asked with feigned nonchalance, "So... Hanguang-jun, have you ever thought about going into seclusion? Retiring from the cultivator world entirely?"

Lan Wangji paused slightly, as if pondering the thought.

Striking while the iron was hot, Wei Wuxian pressed on, "Have you thought about what you’d do after retiring?"

Lan Wangji looked at him. "I haven't."

Perfect!Wei Wuxian thought gleefully.I've already planned it out for you!

He’d find a quiet, scenic spot nestled in the mountains, surrounded by lush greenery, and build a large house. He could build a cozy cottage right next door for Lan Wangji, too. They’d keep things simple—two dishes and a soup every day. Naturally, it would be best if Lan Wangji did the cooking; otherwise, they’d be stuck eating his own lethal culinary creations. Lan Wangji could handle the finances, too.

Wei Wuxian could already picture it: Lan Wangji dressed in coarse, patched-up robes, sitting expressionlessly at a rustic wooden table, counting coins one by one before heading out into the fields with a hoe over his shoulder.

And as for himself... what would he be doing?

Wei Wuxian gave it some serious thought. People always talked about "plowing the fields and weaving cloth." If Lan Wangji was handling the farming, that left the weaving to him. But the image of himself sitting at a loom, crossing his legs and fidgeting nervously, sent an absolute chill down his spine. No, no—he’d better take the hoe instead. Weaving suited Lan Wangji’s steady hands much better.

By day, they’d farm and fish; by night, they’d grab their swords and head out night-hunting to slay monsters. If they ever got bored of the peaceful life, they could just pretend they never retired and re-enter the cultivation world.

Though... it really felt like something was missing. A little one...

Lan Wangji’s voice suddenly broke his reverie. "A little what?"

"Huh?"

Realizing he had accidentally blurted out his last thought, Wei Wuxian quickly straightened his posture, putting on a deadpan face. "I said... Little Apple needs a little friend."

Little Apple whipped his head around and spat forcefully on the ground.

Wei Wuxian smacked the donkey's head playfully, tugging on its long ears with a laugh. But the laughter died in his throat a second later.

He remembered. Years ago, he reallydidhave a little kid trailing behind him here. If the boy had lived to see today, he’d be a teenager by now.

The Burial Mounds were nestled deep within the mountain ranges of Yiling.

People said the Burial Mounds was a mountain built entirely of corpses—that if you took a shovel and dug anywhere on its slopes, you'd unearth a skeleton. The rumors were no exaggeration. It had originally been an ancient battlefield, and for centuries after, locals used it as a dumping ground for unidentified bodies. The thick, stagnant resentment and dark energy had settled into the land, making it a living nightmare for everyone in the region.

As if permanently stained by this malevolence, even the trees on the mountain bore pitch-black leaves. Surrounding the entire base of the mountain was a stone barrier over ten feet tall, its surface covered in densely carved warding talismans to keep both the living and the dead from crossing. This wall had originally been erected by the third-generation sect leader of the Qishan Wen Clan. Unable to purify the overwhelming horde of vengeful spirits, he had settled for containment instead.

Wei Wuxian had personally torn that wall down once in the past. The barrier standing here today was a reinforced replacement built by the Lanling Jin Clan.

Yet when they arrived at the foot of the mountain, they found a massive section of the grand wall collapsed once again.
